statement: A normal menstrual cycle usually lasts between 21 and 35 days.
Menstrual irregularity refers to any noticeable deviation from a woman's normal menstrual pattern.
Amenorrhea means the complete absence of menstruation for three or more consecutive cycles.
Menorrhagia refers to unusually heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding.
Psychological stress can cause menstrual irregularities.
Excessive physical exercise can disrupt the regularity of the menstrual cycle.
Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome (PCOS) is a common cause of irregular periods.
Sudden weight loss or weight gain can affect menstrual regularity.
Irregular periods are always a normal part of student life and never need medical attention.
Use of certain hormonal contraceptives can change a woman's normal menstrual pattern.
Menstrual irregularities may be a sign of an underlying hormonal imbalance.
